outcome: Define Oracle's source-provider topology for repository, accepted artifact, semantic-code, lexical-search, context-graph and future external sources, including a bounded retrieval-planner seam that avoids model-visible provider/tool explosion.
currentProblem: The old BB-062 only mapped repositoryReader and artifactReader and treated MCP as a possible adapter. Runtime Context Intelligence needs evidence-backed semantic code retrieval, indexed search and graph/context sources while preserving distinct source identity and avoiding a generic provider registry that becomes an uncontrolled tool surface.
constraints: Provider capability metadata stays below Oracle; Core/Application request semantics rather than selecting concrete tools.
Repository, accepted artifact, semantic-code/index and graph sources preserve their distinct source identity, provenance and currentness semantics.
Research must evaluate LSP/symbol retrieval, indexed lexical search and graph/context approaches rather than assuming one retrieval family is sufficient.
MCP, if used, is a transport/capability adapter below Oracle and owns no work lifecycle, acceptance or planning authority.
Public GitHub examples used as reusable evidence must have at least 1,000 stars at the research check; otherwise the exception must be explicit.
Reuse, adaptation and in-house seams must be compared on licensing, integration cost, update/currentness behavior and failure modes.
successCriteria: Research defines a provider capability model that can add one source without expanding the caller-facing semantic contract.
Serena/LSP, Zoekt-style indexed search, Aider repo-map patterns and graph/context approaches are compared on the same representative retrieval problems.
A retrieval-planner seam consumes ContextRequirement plus budget and emits bounded provider work without becoming application scheduling authority.
An executable experiment measures relevance/recall, context bytes or tokens, latency, setup/update cost and provenance completeness.
Future external/MCP-backed sources can be adapted without bypassing source identity/currentness checks.
